title: Many Branches
goal: In this lesson you will practice longer if, elif, and else chains that pick one outcome out of many choices.
learn: Keep conditions in a careful order
Use else as the catch all
idea: When there are many options, you can stack several elif lines. Python still only runs one branch, and it is the first one that is True. Think of a menu or a ranking chart. You check the top ranks first, then the next, and finish with a final else for everything that did not match. Clear messages in each branch also make the program easier to follow.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change choice = 3 to choice = 9 and press Run. You should see Unknown choice.

practice.text: Build a day picker. Set day = 6. If 1 print Mon, elif 2 Tue, elif 3 Wed, elif 4 Thu, elif 5 Fri, elif 6 Sat, elif 7 Sun, else Invalid.
practice.hint: Use if day == 1: for Monday and stack an elif for each other number. Python runs only the first match, so with day = 6 you want the Sat branch.
practice.starterTip: Try if day == 1: with print("Mon") indented under it, then elif day == 2: with print("Tue"), and keep going through day 7. Finish with else: and print("Invalid").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if Sat prints for day 6 with a multi-elif chain.

practice.text: Set hp = 12. If hp > 50 print Fine, elif hp > 20 print Wounded, elif hp > 0 print Critical, else print Down.
practice.hint: Check from the highest hp band down. Put hp > 50 first and then the smaller limits, so 12 skips Fine and Wounded and lands on Critical.
practice.starterTip: Try if hp > 50: with print("Fine"), then elif hp > 20: with print("Wounded"), then elif hp > 0: with print("Critical"), and else: with print("Down").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if Critical prints; order of thresholds matters.

quiz.question: In a long if/elif/else chain, how many branches run?
quiz.wrong: Only one True branch runs (or the else), and then Python stops.

quiz.question: What is else for in a menu chain?
quiz.correct: Yes, else handles anything the other checks did not match.
quiz.wrong: When no if or elif matched, the else runs.

quiz.question: Why put higher thresholds first (like >= 90 before >= 80)?

options.text: So a high score is not caught by a lower band

quiz.correct: Right, the first match wins, so a high score has to be checked first.
quiz.wrong: A score of 95 would match >= 80 if that check came first.
